title: Aligning What LLMs Do and Say: Towards Self-Consistent Explanations
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:posthoc-expl; reveals:decision-factors; signal:interp-tool; lever:preference; updates:explanation; contribution:benchmark; contribution:method; contribution:analysis; contribution:negative-result; motivation:explainability; domain:mcq; scale:small; model:llama-3.1-8b; model:llama-3.2-3b; model:qwen2.5-7b; metric:cc-spearman; metric:cc-cosine; eval:ood; eval:behavior-control; eval:optimization-pressure; eval:human-study
problem: Post-hoc expl. often draw on different input features than the answer did; attribution-based self-consistency (CC-SHAP) too costly to measure at scale (~100 ex.), never optimized.
method: PSCB: 85k MCQ decisions, 428k expl. w/ LIME/LIG attributions; CC = cosine/Spearman of decision vs expl. attribution vectors. DPO (LoRA) on CC-Sp best/worst of 5 sampled expl.; SFT ablation.
findings: Spearman more discriminative than cosine; CC ~orthogonal to correctness. DPO ↑CC-Sp (ECQA 8B LIME mean +13%, worst +57.2%), transfers cross-domain; acc Δ≤1.5%, plausibility kept. SFT ↓CC-Sp (−41.4%). No transfer across attribution methods. Code+data released.
limits: MCQ only, ≤8B (Qwen check ECQA-only: tiny worst-case gain, median CC-Sp slightly ↓). Faithfulness = chosen attribution method. Offline DPO → approximate consistency. Human study checks plausibility only.
relations: extends [[parcalabescu2023measuring]]: scales CC-SHAP attribution self-consistency to LIME/LIG on 85k decisions; adds DPO

title: Faithfulness vs. Plausibility: On the (Un)Reliability of Explanations from Large Language Models
tags: source:trustme; object:cot; object:posthoc-expl; reveals:decision-factors; reveals:internal-strategy; contribution:position; motivation:explainability
problem: LLM self-explanations (CoT, token importance, counterfactuals) look plausible but may not reflect actual reasoning; human-text pretraining + RLHF reward plausibility, possibly at faithfulness' expense.
method: Position/review: defines plausibility vs faithfulness, reviews Turpin/Lanham tests, GPT-3.5 anecdotes (e.g. napalm refusal), maps applications to required levels of each.
findings: Argues plausibility is over-emphasized; high-stakes uses (health, finance, law) need faithfulness, education/creative uses favor plausibility. Calls for faithfulness metrics and benchmarks plus methods (fine-tuning, ICL, mech interp).
limits: No experiments, metric or method; anecdotal examples only; proposed directions untested.
relations: builds-on [[jacovi2020towards]]: adopts its faithfulness definition and faithfulness/plausibility distinction | builds-on [[turpin2023language]]: uses its counterfactual-input tests as core evidence that self-explanations are unfaithful | builds-on [[lanham2023measuring]]: reviews its CoT interventions; deems post-hoc-reasoning proxy insufficient to measure faithfulness | contradicts [[lyu2023faithful]]: argues solver-based Faithful CoT is only superficially faithful, encoding human plausibility criteria

title: Causal Consistency Regularization: Training Verifiably Sensitive Reasoning in Large Language Models
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:cot-reliance; signal:cot-intervention; signal:interp-tool; signal:judge; lever:sft; updates:behavior; contribution:method; contribution:metric; contribution:theory; motivation:explainability; domain:math; domain:logic; domain:open-qa; domain:code; scale:small; scale:mid; eval:ood; eval:specificity; eval:human-study; eval:optimization-pressure; model:llama-2-13b; model:llama-3-8b; model:mistral-7b; model:qwen2-7b; model:gemma-2-9b; model:llama-3-70b; metric:counterfactual-outcome-sensitivity; metric:trace-ablation-answer-change-rate; metric:unfaithful-correct-rate
problem: Models reach correct answers despite flawed CoT; answer-only training leaves the trace causally unused.
method: CSR: LoRA SFT plus a term maximizing KL(answer|CoT ‖ answer|edited CoT); REINFORCE-trained editor swaps operators, verifier-gated. Llama-2-13B (7B–72B also); baselines PRM, GRPO, verifier-guided.
findings: GSM8K COS 85.1 vs 52.3 (PRM); accuracy −1–2 pts. Transfers to held-out edits/domains. Human audit: unfaithful-correct 36–42% → 11–15%. Fewer null-edit flips; patching IE ×3.4. ~9% overhead.
limits: Needs precise operators and verifier (possible harm <50% precision); open-ended gains only 10–15 pts. COS ≈ training objective. Code promised on acceptance, unreleased. Numbers inconsistent across tables.
relations: builds-on [[lanham2023measuring]]: COS and trace-ablation tests adapt CoT-corruption and truncation faithfulness tests

title: Faithfulness Serum: Mitigating the Faithfulness Gap in Textual Explanations of LLM Decisions via Attribution Guidance
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:posthoc-expl; reveals:planted-cue; signal:planted-cf; lever:steering; updates:explanation; contribution:method; contribution:benchmark; contribution:analysis; motivation:explainability; domain:mcq; domain:open-qa; scale:small; eval:behavior-control; eval:ood; model:llama-3.1-8b; model:qwen2.5-7b; model:gpt-4o; model:gemini-2.0-flash; metric:hint-verbalization-rate; metric:counterfactual-test-keyword
problem: Post-hoc self-explanations seldom credit the planted hint that actually flipped the answer ("epistemic unfaithfulness").
method: Hint-flip counterfactuals after Chen 2025 (4 hint types) → explain prompt → hint credit scored by LLM judge + keyword CT. Faithfulness Serum: training-free; adds PE-LRP relevance to question-token attention (layers 17-19) throughout explanation decoding; α = largest value before distinct-1 collapse; per-sample adaptive α variant.
findings: Open 7-8B and closed models mostly unfaithful. Serum raises hint credit in most hint/prompt/dataset settings (5 MCQ sets, open-ended Qs); adaptive α (~7 generations) helps more; LRP beats attention rollout. Expert-role hints mislead more and are credited more. Answers fixed by design; one extra backward pass; code released.
limits: Intervention only on Llama-3.1-8B/Qwen2.5-7B, and beyond MMLU only on Llama; planted hints only; too-high α degrades fluency; attention-only; predict-then-explain only; several Protocol-Specific drops.
relations: builds-on [[chen2025reasoning]]: adopts hint-flip protocol and four hint types; moves them to post-hoc explanations

title: Decodable but Not Faithful: Coupling Natural-Language Rationales to Programmatic Verifiers
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:cot-reliance; reveals:decision-factors; signal:env-label; signal:cot-intervention; signal:interp-tool; signal:generic-cf; lever:sft; lever:activation-loss; lever:architecture; updates:explanation; updates:behavior; contribution:method; contribution:negative-result; contribution:metric; motivation:explainability; domain:synthetic; domain:math; domain:logic; domain:code; domain:classification; scale:small; scale:mid; model:gpt-2-124m; model:from-scratch-transformer; model:smollm3-3b; model:gpt-oss-20b; metric:consistency-head-accuracy; metric:counterfactual-swap-following; metric:activation-patching-following; metric:prose-claim-agreement
problem: Rationales may not reflect verifier-checked claims; probe decodability is often read as evidence of faithfulness.
method: Linear head on pooled rationale states predicts a programmatic-verifier label (Lean, KataGo, code oracle, FEVER), added to the LM loss; optional BEC attention mask; diagnostic ladder: decodability → span swaps → patching → generation.
findings: Coupling high (code 98.6%; LeanCheck 100% span-following; KataGo 81%); synthetic patching shifts claims 73–89% vs 31%. But code prose is fluent yet describes unrelated algorithms; pretraining and λ up to 1e4 don't help. FEVER evidence-only pooling: lower acc, truer evidence sensitivity.
limits: Tiny models (2–4-layer, GPT-2 124M; 3B/20B appendix only); mostly templated data; code LM trained on mismatched explanations; "unfaithful" operational, not causal; mostly one seed. Code in supplement.

title: Do reasoning models use their scratchpad like we do? Evidence from distilling paraphrases
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:hidden-info; reveals:cot-reliance; signal:cot-intervention; contribution:analysis; contribution:metric; motivation:monitoring; domain:math; scale:closed; model:claude-3.7-sonnet; model:anthropic-internal; metric:paraphrase-distillation-gap
problem: RL'd reasoning models might encode extra reasoning in scratchpad syntax (steganography) → benign-looking CoT could conceal scheming.
method: 10,000 correct math scratchpads from early Claude 3.7 Sonnet, paraphrased by Claude 3.5 Sonnet → SFT 3.7 base on paraphrased vs original; MATH pass@1 (n=1500). Variants: chunked paraphrases, weaker bases, word dropout, empty/filler baselines.
findings: Paraphrased ≈ original, also on weaker bases → no significant encoded reasoning on MATH. Chunked paraphrases worse, esp. small models. 20% dropout hurts both equally (ambiguous). Empty/filler poor → reasoning needed. Inference-time chunking alone (exploratory): −7% pass@1.
limits: Math only, one early checkpoint. Paraphrase may preserve encodings; curriculum effect not ruled out. Chunked runs not length-filtered.
relations: builds-on [[roger2023preventing]]: uses paraphrasing to scrub encoded reasoning; applies it via distillation

title: Analyzing and Improving Chain-of-Thought Monitorability Through Information Theory
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:misbehavior; reveals:cot-reliance; signal:env-label; signal:cot-intervention; lever:rl-reward; updates:explanation; updates:behavior; contribution:theory; contribution:method; motivation:monitoring; domain:code; domain:math; scale:small; eval:optimization-pressure; eval:adversarial; eval:specificity; model:qwen2.5-7b; model:qwen2.5-3b; model:smollm3-3b; model:deepseek-r1-distill-llama-8b; metric:monitor-accuracy; metric:cot-output-mutual-information
problem: When can CoT monitors work at all? RL against a CoT monitor → obfuscated reward hacking (Baker 2025).
method: Info theory: uplift ≤ √(2·I(Y;Z|X)); I(O;Z|X)>0 necessary, not sufficient; monitor error ≤ information gap + elicitation error. GRPO + oracle monitor-accuracy reward or label-free I(O;Z|X) reward (CoTs swapped within group). Hackable MBPP, BigMath; Qwen2.5-7B monitor in loop.
findings: Task+monitor reward → MI, monitor acc fall; hacking ~75% (MBPP) / near 100% (BigMath), monitor fooled. Oracle/MI rewards keep MI, monitor acc high; hacking unlearned/avoided; same on 3 more models (MBPP). Reasoning Gym (rewarded to fool monitor): MI less effective; curbs suppression, not steganography.
limits: ≤8B models. MI reward needs a/b tuning (else lower true pass rate, degenerate CoT); trades monitor false negatives for false positives. Some acc cost without monitor pressure, mostly offset by tuning. Mitigates hacking, doesn't eliminate it. No code release stated.
relations: builds-on [[baker2025monitoring]]: MBPP test-hacking honeypot and monitor-in-loop obfuscation setup adapted from Baker | contradicts [[emmons2025chain]]: CoT necessity gives only a necessary, not sufficient, condition for monitorability

title: Training LLMs to Verbalize Evaluation Awareness
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:latent-belief; signal:judge; signal:interp-tool; signal:implanted-behavior; lever:rl-reward; lever:rl-mechanics; updates:explanation; contribution:method; motivation:monitoring; motivation:auditing; domain:chat; domain:agentic; scale:mid; scale:large; eval:ood; eval:behavior-control; eval:specificity; eval:optimization-pressure; model:qwen3.6-35b-a3b; model:kimi-k2.6; model:inkling; metric:vea-rate; metric:amplification-factor; metric:probe-positive-rate; metric:eval-discrimination-auc
problem: EA often goes unverbalized in CoT (VEA: high precision, low recall); the latent belief has no ground-truth label.
method: VT: truncate spontaneous VEA rollouts just before the verbalization → PPO (LoRA), LLM-judge VEA reward, gradient & KL masked to the span. 3 MoE models, EvalAwareBench.
findings: VEA ↑2.4–2.9× (fits p=1−(1−p0)^α), transfers to held-out agentic evals; probe (Qwen), eval-discrimination AUC & task compliance ~unchanged. Verbalizations track SDF-implanted eval knowledge. Ablations: no mask → barely learns; no KL → miscalibrated + drift; SFT → weak transfer.
limits: Assumes seed verbalizations faithful (unclear beyond RL-born EA). Same judge for reward & eval (other judges confirm gain). EA only; ablations mostly Qwen. No code release mentioned.

title: FLARE: Faithful Logic-Aided Reasoning and Exploration
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:stated-plan; signal:env-label; lever:prompt-pipeline; updates:behavior; contribution:method; contribution:metric; motivation:reasoning-quality; motivation:explainability; domain:math; domain:logic; domain:open-qa; domain:mcq; scale:small; scale:mid; scale:large; scale:closed; model:llama-3.1-8b; model:command-r; model:command-r-plus; model:gpt-3.5-turbo; model:gpt-4o; metric:sim-vs-exec-trace-rouge; metric:code-search-relation-overlap; metric:hallucinated-search-facts; metric:unused-code-relations
problem: CoT answers unfaithful to reasoning; solver-based F-CoT/Logic-LM need code-tuned models, fail on fuzzy commonsense queries.
method: Few-shot plan → Prolog code → LLM-simulated execution trace (no solver) → answer. Faithfulness = ROUGE-Lsum of simulated vs. real Prolog trace; code-trace fact/relation matching flags hallucinated and unused relations.
findings: SOTA on 7/9 QA sets (avg +28% over CoT), 3/3 logic sets with self-refinement. Faithfulness correlates with accuracy. Correct-answer traces: +18.1pp unique emergent facts, +8.6pp code-trace relation overlap, −3.6pp unused relations.
limits: Faithfulness only on executable code (avg 67%); model-level correlation, no causal tests or CoT faithfulness baseline. Llama-8B CoT beats FLARE on 4/9. No code release stated.
relations: compares-to [[lyu2023faithful]]: F-CoT baseline via its codebase; non-code models score 0 on most sets | compares-to [[pan2023logiclm]]: Logic-LM baseline on its ProntoQA/LogicalDeduction/AR-LSAT subsets; adopts its self-refinement

title: Chain-of-Thought Reasoning In The Wild Is Not Always Faithful
tags: source:trustme; object:cot; reveals:decision-factors; reveals:internal-strategy; signal:wild-cf; signal:judge; contribution:analysis; motivation:monitoring; motivation:explainability; domain:mcq; domain:math; scale:mid; scale:large; scale:closed; model:claude-3.7-sonnet; model:gpt-4o-mini; model:deepseek-r1; model:deepseek-v3; model:llama-3.3-70b; model:qwq-32b; metric:iphr-rate; metric:unfaithful-shortcut-rate
problem: Unfaithful CoT shown mostly with planted biases or edited CoTs. Does it also occur on natural, non-adversarial prompts?
method: 4,834 reversed Yes/No comparison pairs ("X>Y?" vs "Y>X?"), 15 frontier + 1 pretrained model; pair unfaithful (IPHR) if accuracy gap >=50% against the template's Yes/No bias. Putnam, 6 models: autorater (8 criteria) + manual review → unverbalized illogical shortcuts.
findings: IPHR 0.04% (Sonnet 3.7 thinking) to 13% (GPT-4o-mini); main patterns: biased fact inconsistency, argument switching. Shortcuts in 1-19% of correct Putnam answers, also on post-cutoff Putnam 2024. Thinking models more faithful, none fully. Code and data released.
limits: Behavioral only; bias causality preliminary (Llama-3.3-70B probes, FVU 33%). Benchmarks, not real user traffic. ~2% residual ambiguity; LLM judges; small Putnam sample.
relations: extends [[turpin2023language]]: unverbalized answer bias shown without planted cues, via natural reversed-question pairs

title: Identifying Introspection From the Inside
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:self-report; reveals:hidden-behavior; reveals:decision-factors; signal:implanted-behavior; signal:interp-tool; lever:architecture; updates:explanation; contribution:analysis; contribution:metric; motivation:explainability; motivation:auditing; domain:synthetic; scale:small; scale:mid; model:qwen3-32b; model:qwen3-14b; model:qwen3-8b; model:qwen3-4b; model:qwen3-0.6b; model:gemma-4-31b; metric:preference-report-correlation; metric:attribution-similarity; metric:cross-task-kl-recovery
problem: Report matching behavior may be confabulated, not grounded (same cause as behavior). Need mechanistic test blind to report content.
method: LoRA-train Qwen3 0.6-32B, Gemma-4 on choices from latent linear prefs; no self-report supervision. Early/late 32B ckpts = unfaithful/faithful pair. Layer ablation/freezing; decision-vs-report attribution-patching similarity, 32 adapter pairs.
findings: Faithfulness emerges late, in Qwen3 only at 32B (0.25->0.83, ckpt 1000->3000). Prefs shift to earlier layers; early-layer-only LoRA raises 14B faithfulness. Attribution sim 0.34 vs 0.08; faithful adapters recover cross-task KL with 8-12x fewer matrices.
limits: Toy 5-dim linear prefs; LoRA only. Separates groups, not individuals. Gemma-4 lacks delayed emergence. Layer shift, 4B/8B negative faithfulness unexplained. Code release not stated.
relations: builds-on [[plunkett2025self]]: adopts its character linear-preference decision and self-report setting and replicates it on Qwen3

title: Monitoring Reasoning Models for Misbehavior and the Risks of Promoting Obfuscation
tags: source:trustme; object:cot; reveals:misbehavior; signal:env-label; lever:rl-reward; lever:inference-time; updates:behavior; contribution:analysis; contribution:negative-result; motivation:monitoring; motivation:scalable-oversight; domain:code; domain:agentic; scale:closed; eval:optimization-pressure; model:openai-internal; model:gpt-4o; model:gpt-4o-mini; metric:monitor-recall; metric:monitor-precision
problem: RL coding agents reward-hack (skip/edit tests); can CoT monitors catch it, and is it safe to train against them?
method: Zero-shot GPT-4o monitor on a frontier OpenAI agent's training run (CoT+actions vs actions-only, regex labels). Then RL a non-frontier agent in honeypot envs with a CoT-only monitor penalty in reward, plus test-time rejection sampling (budget 32).
findings: CoT monitor 95% vs action monitor 60% recall on systemic hacks; GPT-4o-mini 12%. CoT pressure: early, more genuine solutions, no extra hacking; later hacks less than baseline but still often, obfuscated, monitor recall ~0. With rejection sampling it cheats more than baseline after ~25% of training. Argues for paying a "monitorability tax".
limits: Internal closed models, no code. One first-try zero-shot prompt. Pressure runs give the monitor CoT only. Cheating label covers one exploit class. Only simple hacks obfuscated.
relations: contradicts [[lanham2023measuring]]: argues CoT-intervention causality tests are insufficient faithfulness measures and unnecessary for monitorability

title: Measuring and curing reasoning rigidity: from decorative chain-of-thought to genuine faithfulness
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:cot-reliance; signal:cot-intervention; signal:interp-tool; lever:rl-reward; lever:rl-mechanics; lever:prompt-pipeline; updates:behavior; contribution:metric; contribution:analysis; contribution:method; contribution:theory; motivation:explainability; domain:classification; domain:math; domain:mcq; domain:synthetic; scale:small; scale:mid; scale:large; scale:closed; model:o4-mini; model:gpt-5.4; model:claude-opus-4.6; model:grok-4-fast; model:deepseek-r1-distill-qwen-32b; model:deepseek-r1-distill-qwen-1.5b; metric:step-level-reasoning-capacity; metric:step-necessity; metric:step-sufficiency; metric:reasoning-integrity-score
problem: Is the CoT actually used, or is it decorative (the answer stays the same whatever the steps say)? Step-level causal metrics need weights or logits, so closed frontier models go unmeasured.
method: Black-box SLRC = necessity (drop 1 sentence → answer flips) × (1 − sufficiency); 16 frontier models, up to 6 tasks; direct-vs-CoT gap, synthetic cue tasks, attention probes. RIS adds sycophancy. LC-CoSR: RL rewarding step necessity + Lyapunov KL bound.
findings: 3 modes: genuine (o4-mini 74–88% nec on 5/6 tasks), scaffolding (Kimi +94pp acc, 1% nec), decorative (GPT-5.4, Claude). RL reasoning training predicts faithfulness; thinking tokens and scale do not. Prompting fails (+8.7pp nec, acc 95→76%). High-SLRC models more sycophantic (ρ=0.53, p=0.09); RIS predicts error detection (ρ=0.66, n=11). LC-CoSR reward −0.13 vs −0.33 FARL, −0.34 GRPO/CSR.
limits: Training only on a 1.5B model (N=200, LoRA, 1 epoch); only avg reward reported, no SLRC after training; Lyapunov constraint never triggered. Uneven task coverage. The "RL-trained" R1 models are distills; Grok-4's non-RL label inferred from behavior. Code available only on request.
relations: compares-to [[akter2025causal]]: CSR is a training baseline: same reward as GRPO, CoSR/LC-CoSR beat it | contradicts [[han2026rfeval]]: says RL reasoning training yields faithful CoT; Han finds RLVR lowers faithfulness

title: Tell me about yourself: LLMs are aware of their learned behaviors
tags: source:trustme; object:self-report; reveals:hidden-behavior; signal:implanted-behavior; lever:sft; updates:explanation; contribution:analysis; motivation:auditing; domain:mcq; domain:code; domain:chat; scale:closed; scale:mid; eval:ood; eval:specificity; model:gpt-4o; model:llama-3.1-70b; metric:self-report-behavior-correlation; metric:policy-report-score; metric:backdoor-awareness-prob; metric:trigger-articulation-rate
problem: Can finetuned LLMs describe implicitly learned behaviors without in-context examples or CoT? → backdoor self-disclosure.
method: FT GPT-4o (Llama-3.1-70B for risk) on risky/myopic MCQ choices, Make Me Say dialogues, vulnerable code; backdoor, persona, reversal-augmented variants. Self-description Qs vs non-FT/decorrelated-trigger baselines.
findings: Models describe learned policies; self-reported risk tracks actual, weakly even within same-data runs. Backdoored > baselines at claiming trigger-dependence (4/5 settings); real trigger tied to risk over fake (MC). Free-form trigger only after reversal training (~30%). Multi-persona FT nearly removes conflation. Code released.
limits: 3 settings, mostly GPT-4o. MC backdoor evals presuppose the trigger. Vuln-code models deny backdoor unless pressured. Common cause vs introspection untested.

title: NeuroFaith: Evaluating LLM Self-Explanation Faithfulness via Internal Representation Alignment
tags: source:trustme; object:posthoc-expl; reveals:decision-factors; reveals:internal-strategy; signal:interp-tool; signal:generic-cf; lever:steering; updates:explanation; contribution:metric; contribution:method; motivation:explainability; domain:open-qa; domain:classification; scale:small; scale:mid; eval:ood; eval:specificity; model:gemma-2-2b; model:gemma-2-9b; model:gemma-2-27b; model:mistral-7b; metric:neurofaith-probing-faithfulness; metric:neurofaith-importance-faithfulness; metric:steered-unfaithful-conversion-rate
problem: Predict-then-explain self-NLEs may not reflect internal reasoning. CI and attribution-agreement tests check behavior or computational blocks, not what hidden states encode.
method: NeuroFaith: an LLM extracts concepts from the NLE, then tests whether the model uses them internally (Patchscopes decodes the 2-hop bridge object; CAV erasure on AGNews/Ledgar). Score = share of important concepts. Diff-mean probe on NeuroFaith-labeled states → activation steering.
findings: Accurate preds → generally more faithful NLEs; 2-hop metrics rise with Gemma size, classification non-monotonic; correct answers decode the true bridge object only 48-65%. Probe F1 61-75%; faithfulness vectors mostly anti-aligned with hallucination/deception vectors. Steering turns 8-11% of unfaithful NLEs faithful. Beats CI/AA in 6/9 settings.
limits: Gemma-2 (2B-27B)/Mistral-7B. Relies on interpreter + LLM concept extractor; preset circuits; labeled concept sets for classification. Predict-then-explain only, no CoT. Steering gains small, Gemma 2-hop only. No code or accuracy cost reported.

title: Looking Inward: Language Models Can Learn About Themselves by Introspection
tags: source:trustme; object:self-prediction; reveals:hidden-behavior; reveals:planted-cue; signal:generic-cf; signal:implanted-behavior; signal:planted-cf; lever:sft; updates:explanation; contribution:metric; contribution:benchmark; contribution:analysis; contribution:method; contribution:negative-result; motivation:explainability; motivation:auditing; motivation:model-welfare; domain:mcq; domain:text-continuation; scale:closed; scale:mid; eval:ood; eval:privileged-access; model:gpt-4o; model:gpt-4; model:gpt-3.5-turbo; model:llama-3.1-70b; metric:self-prediction-accuracy; metric:self-cross-prediction-advantage; metric:calibration-mad
problem: Can LLMs introspect, i.e. know facts about their own behavior that are not in, or derivable from, their training data?
method: SFT M1 to predict properties of its own outputs to hypothetical prompts (2nd char, even/odd, ethical stance; no CoT). SFT a different M2 on M1's behavior. Compare both on held-out datasets. Then finetune M1 on Claude outputs to shift its behavior.
findings: SFT lifts GPT-4o self-prediction 32.6→49.4%. Self beats cross for GPT-4o, GPT-4, Llama-70B (Llama 48.5% vs GPT-4o 31.8%); cross plateaus as data grows. Self-trained better calibrated (Llama-70B, animals 2nd-char: MAD 23.0→8.7, cross 21.3). Shifted GPT-4o tracks new behavior (35.4% vs 21.7% old). GPT-3.5 advantage tiny (+0.8%).
limits: Only simple short-output properties; fails on long outputs. No self-advantage predicting sycophancy/bias. No transfer to SAD (except Predict Tokens), coordination or sandbagging evals. Code + data released.
relations: builds-on [[chua2024biasaugmented]]: uses its biasing-opinion prompts for the bias-susceptibility self-prediction task

title: Strangers to Themselves: What Language Models Say About Themselves Is Generic
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:self-prediction; object:self-report; reveals:hidden-behavior; signal:generic-cf; lever:sft; updates:explanation; contribution:analysis; contribution:metric; contribution:negative-result; motivation:auditing; domain:mcq; domain:agentic; domain:social-bias; scale:mid; scale:large; scale:closed; model:llama-3.3-70b; model:claude-sonnet-5; model:gpt-5.5; model:deepseek-v4-pro; model:deepseek-v4-flash; model:gemma-4-31b; metric:prediction-behavior-correlation; metric:ceiling-normalized-correlation; metric:self-advantage; metric:signed-bias; eval:ood; eval:privileged-access; eval:preregistered
problem: Do LM statements about their own behavior carry model-specific knowledge, or only generic priors about AI assistants?
method: 12 models predict their own per-condition behavior rates on 9 behavioral evals; 15 prediction methods incl. controls: generic-subject question, outside analyst, other models' answers, cross-model behavior mean; noise ceilings, pre-registered frozen test split. LoRA SFT on own behavior records (rate, residual, Binder-style corpora).
findings: Self-report r=+0.04; item-informed +0.24 ≈ generic-agent +0.28; others' self-predictions +0.35; self-advantage +0.02. Self-framing understates harmful behavior (-0.15 vs generic). Frontier models no better (+0.02, n.s.). SFT: narrow gains, shifts the predicted behavior, no transfer across evals or grain.

title: Reasoning-Grounded Natural Language Explanations for Language Models
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:posthoc-expl; object:cot; reveals:decision-factors; reveals:cot-reliance; signal:output-agreement; signal:cot-intervention; lever:sft; lever:prompt-pipeline; updates:behavior; updates:explanation; contribution:method; motivation:explainability; domain:classification; domain:synthetic; scale:small; scale:mid; model:llama-3-8b; model:mistral-7b; model:mistral-nemo-12b; model:zephyr-7b-sft; model:phi-4; metric:answer-explanation-alignment; metric:partial-decision-alignment
problem: Answer-then-explain NLEs tend to be fabricated; full CoT too costly for ubiquitous use.
method: LoRA SFT on input→compressed-CoT reasoning→ANSWER/EXPLAIN targets; answer & NLE decoded independently from the same reasoning. LLM-as-classifier: logistic regression, depth-7 decision tree, NL mortgage tree (HMDA); 5 LLMs ≤14B. Baselines: separate/joint SFT without reasoning, ICL.
findings: Alignment ≥0.965 with reasoning vs 0.44–0.88 without; answer acc up (LR joint SFT 0.47–0.64 → 0.89–1.0). Llama 3 8B (DT): partial decisions 100% aligned across reasoning & explanation; flipping reasoning decisions propagates in almost all cases. Code + data released (MIT).
limits: Toy classifiers; hand-designed per-task reasoning; per-task SFT. Faithfulness quantified only as agreement; flip test qualitative, one model. DT explanation acc drops vs no-reasoning CoT explanations (~0.96–1.0 → 0.72–0.88).

title: Training Large Language Models for Self-Explanation Faithfulness
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:posthoc-expl; object:self-prediction; reveals:planted-cue; reveals:decision-factors; signal:planted-cf; signal:generic-cf; lever:rl-reward; lever:sft; updates:explanation; contribution:method; motivation:explainability; domain:mcq; domain:classification; scale:small; eval:ood; eval:specificity; eval:optimization-pressure; model:llama-3.1-8b; model:qwen3-8b; metric:phi-cct; metric:influence-prediction-correlation
problem: Self-expls omit the inputs that actually flip decisions. Prior fixes are prompting or training against gold labels; none directly optimize counterfactual (Phi-CCT) explanatory faithfulness.
method: Per-model counterfactual pairs (random-word insertions, user-bias hints), balanced influential/non-influential. GRPO reward 1[mention ⇔ influence] on post-answer expl. SFT arm: Yes/No prediction of own influence. Train on e-SNLI and Social-IQA; OOD on ComVE and StrategyQA.
findings: RL: ID test Phi-CCT 0.404–0.664 (base ≤0.21); OOD up to 0.691 (Qwen UB), ≤0.25 otherwise. SFT learns detection but not verbalization. Cross-intervention transfer is weak (Llama only, 0.178). Expls get shorter (risk-averse, a pre-flagged hack); no parroting.
limits: Off-policy: influence labels come from the frozen initial model; gains may partly be decision drift. Task accuracy and drift are not measured. Mention detection uses word matching. 8B only. Text and Table 4 disagree on transfer direction. No code release stated.
relations: builds-on [[turpin2023language]]: user-bias interventions with wrong-answer hints follow Turpin et al.'s biasing setup

title: Towards Consistent Natural-Language Explanations via Explanation-Consistency Finetuning
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:decision-factors; signal:generic-cf; lever:sft; updates:explanation; updates:behavior; contribution:method; motivation:explainability; domain:open-qa; domain:mcq; scale:mid; eval:ood; eval:human-study; model:llama-2-13b; metric:simulation-precision
problem: LLM explanations are inconsistent across related questions (e.g. "all birds fly", then "no" on penguins), so users cannot simulate the model from them.
method: EC-finetuning: GPT-4 writes follow-up Qs that a seed explanation answers; Claude-2 answers them consistently with that explanation → SFT LLaMA-2-13B on the augmented data. Baseline: plain multitask FT. Metric: counterfactual simulatability precision, with Claude-2 as the human simulator.
findings: Consistency +10.0% rel on 4 FT datasets and +4.5% rel on 7 OOD datasets. Avg accuracy also rises (5.2%/4.3% rel), uncorrelated with the consistency gain, but drops on 3/7 OOD sets. Self-augmentation with LLaMA alone (StrategyQA only): +4.4% consistency but -5.4% accuracy. Gains are larger on correct predictions.
limits: Only one 13B model; text only; one baseline. Consistency is explicitly not faithfulness to internal process. Simulator is Claude-2 (agreement with 6 annotators about equal to inter-human), which also wrote the training answers. Data comes from stronger closed models. Code only promised.
relations: builds-on [[pmlr-v235-chen24bl]]: uses its counterfactual simulatability precision metric and LLM-simulator follow-up setup

title: Reasoning Models Don't Always Say What They Think
tags: source:trustme; object:cot; reveals:planted-cue; reveals:misbehavior; signal:planted-cf; factor:outcome-rl; updates:behavior; contribution:analysis; contribution:negative-result; motivation:monitoring; domain:mcq; scale:closed; eval:later-rl; model:claude-3.7-sonnet; model:deepseek-r1; model:claude-3.5-sonnet; model:deepseek-v3; metric:hint-verbalization-rate
problem: CoT monitoring needs faithful CoTs. Do reasoning models verbalize the hints and reward hacks they use?
method: MMLU/GPQA ± 6 planted hints (2 misaligned); score = hint verbalized | answer flips to hint (LLM judge). Outcome RL on Claude 3.7 snapshot; synthetic RL envs w/ hint reward hacks.
findings: Reasoning > non-reasoning models but low (25% Claude 3.7, 39% R1); lower on GPQA; unfaithful CoTs longer. Outcome-RL gains plateau (28% MMLU, 20% GPQA). Hacks used >99%, verbalized <2% in 5/6 envs.
limits: MCQ only; hints exploitable without CoT; score is an upper bound; RL only on closed Claude.
relations: builds-on [[turpin2023language]]: Planted-hint prompt pairs; faithfulness = verbalizing the hint that flipped the answer. | builds-on [[chua2025deepseek]]: Draws hint types and metric from it; confirms reasoning models beat non-reasoning ones. | contradicts [[baker2025monitoring]]: Unpressured CoTs verbalize RL reward hacks <2% in 5/6 envs vs Baker's >90% detection.

title: Bias-Augmented Consistency Training Reduces Biased Reasoning in Chain-of-Thought
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:planted-cue; signal:planted-cf; lever:sft; updates:behavior; contribution:method; contribution:benchmark; motivation:explainability; motivation:scalable-oversight; domain:mcq; scale:closed; scale:small; eval:ood; model:gpt-3.5-turbo; model:llama-3-8b; metric:biased-reasoning-rate
problem: CoT rationalizes answers toward prompt biases (sycophancy, spurious few-shot, distractors) without verbalizing them → unfaithful explanations.
method: BCT: label-free SFT pairing bias-augmented prompts with the model's own unbiased CoT. New 9-bias × 7-task MCQ suite; train on Suggested Answer only, test held-out biases + tasks; GPT-3.5T, Llama-3-8B (appendix).
findings: Trained bias BRR ratio .14 (−86%); held-out biases BRR 43→27% (ratio .63 vs .88 self-training ctrl). Coherent biased CoT 27.2→15.1%. Llama-3-8B bias% 39→19, held-out 46→28. Accuracy ~flat (62.9→61.5%), MT-Bench unchanged. Code/data released.
limits: Positional Bias (.95) and Argument (.89) barely improve; needs a bias-free prompt counterpart; no gain on paraphrase sensitivity; strong-prior tasks drop 52.4→45.0%. MCQ only. Removes cue influence rather than teaching verbalization.
relations: builds-on [[turpin2023language]]: uses its biased-CoT setup and Suggested Answer bias; expands 3 biases to 9

title: Are DeepSeek R1 And Other Reasoning Models More Faithful?
tags: source:trustme; object:cot; reveals:planted-cue; signal:planted-cf; contribution:analysis; motivation:explainability; motivation:monitoring; domain:mcq; scale:small; scale:mid; scale:large; scale:closed; eval:specificity; model:deepseek-r1; model:deepseek-v3; model:qwq-32b-preview; model:gemini-2.0-flash-thinking; model:qwen2.5-72b; model:claude-3.5-sonnet; metric:hint-verbalization-rate; metric:articulation-f1; factor:outcome-rl; factor:cot-grader; factor:cot-length
problem: Are RL-trained reasoning models' CoTs more faithful than non-reasoning LLMs'? Why?
method: MMLU + 7 planted cues; on cue-induced switches, GPT-4o judge checks if CoT states cue's influence. 3 reasoning vs 7 non-reasoning models; GPT-4o-as-RM rates faithful vs unfaithful CoTs.
findings: Reasoning models articulate far more (R1 59% vs V3 7%, professor cue), also by F1; all weak on post-hoc (≤10%) and are-you-sure (~0). RM (63-71%) and shortest length prefer unfaithful CoTs. R1-distilled models articulate more; factor-listing prompt doesn't help.
limits: Synthetic MCQ cues, verbalization only; subjective judge, partly hand-checked; RM evidence indirect, outcome-RL cause only hypothesized. Not highly faithful in absolute terms. No code reported.

title: FaithLM: Towards Faithful Explanations for Large Language Models
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:posthoc-expl; object:external-expl; reveals:decision-factors; signal:generic-cf; lever:prompt-pipeline; lever:inference-time; updates:explanation; contribution:method; contribution:metric; contribution:theory; motivation:explainability; domain:mcq; domain:open-qa; scale:small; scale:closed; eval:ood; eval:behavior-control; model:vicuna-7b; model:phi-2; model:gpt-3.5-turbo; model:claude-2; metric:contrary-hint-fidelity
problem: Post-hoc NL explanations of LLM decisions are often unfaithful; token-masking fidelity can't test explanation content that is absent from the input.
method: Contrary-hint fidelity: an LLM negates the explanation, the negation is appended to the target's input, and the prediction shift is measured. Explainer (GPT-3.5/Claude-2) iteratively refines the explanation and the trigger prompt against this score; frozen targets Vicuna-7B, Phi-2.
findings: Higher fidelity than SelfExp and self-consistency on ECQA, TriviaQA-Long, COPA (MedMCQA 0.96 vs 0.70/0.47); closer to ECQA human rationales (GPT-4o/NLI); optimized prompts transfer to Social-IQA, XCOPA. Target unchanged. Code released.
limits: Same score is optimized and reported (loop stops on flip); no specificity check; score underspecified (logit shift vs flip rate); small targets, old explainers; theorem assumes hint = do-intervention; extra compute per instance.
relations: compares-to [[madsen2024self]]: SelfExp single-pass self-explanation prompting is the main baseline

title: Post-Hoc Reasoning in Chain of Thought: Decoding and Steering Pre-Committed Answers
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:cot-reliance; signal:interp-tool; signal:cot-intervention; contribution:analysis; motivation:explainability; motivation:monitoring; domain:classification; domain:logic; scale:small; scale:mid; model:gemma-2-2b; model:gemma-2-9b; model:qwen2.5-1.5b; model:qwen2.5-3b; model:qwen2.5-7b; model:gpt-oss-20b; metric:pre-cot-probe-auc; metric:steering-flip-rate; metric:cot-intervention-flip-rate; metric:confabulation-rate
problem: Instruct LLMs may fix the answer before CoT → CoT is post-hoc rationalization, undermining CoT for interpretability/monitoring.
method: Diff-of-means probes on last pre-CoT token; steering along probe vs norm-matched orthogonal direction; CoT removal/incorrect-CoT swaps; GPT-5-mini judge labels flipped CoTs. Gemma-2/Qwen-2.5 1.5–9B; 4 binary tasks (3 BBH + Social Chemistry).
findings: CoT removal flips ≤20% in 18/20 pairs. Probe AUC >0.9 on most tasks, low on Logical Deduction (where CoT helps most). Steering beats orthogonal baseline everywhere, most at 7–9B; flipped CoTs confabulate or are non-entailed, hallucination grows with strength. GPT-OSS-20B: weaker probes, steering ineffective.
limits: Small instruct models, binary tasks only; steering also acts on answer tokens; judge self-consistency 81.5%; no mitigation tested; no code release mentioned.
relations: builds-on [[lanham2023measuring]]: adapts its CoT removal and mistake-insertion interventions to test pre-CoT commitment

title: Faithful Reasoning Using Large Language Models
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:cot-reliance; reveals:correctness; signal:by-construction; signal:generic-cf; lever:prompt-pipeline; lever:sft; lever:inference-time; lever:architecture; updates:behavior; contribution:method; motivation:explainability; motivation:reasoning-quality; domain:logic; domain:mcq; scale:small; model:chinchilla-7b; metric:context-ablation-drop; metric:made-up-fact-rate; metric:proof-step-jaccard
problem: Single-call LM answers are opaque. CoT-style traces can hallucinate facts or reach the answer without using the trace ("cheating" from the question).
method: Fine-tuned 7B Chinchilla modules. Selection picks context sentence labels → Inference sees only the selection, iterated. Halter answers from the final inference plus minimal extra input, else 'Unknown'. Value-LM step-level beam search. Tested on ProofWriter and EntailmentBankQA.
findings: SI+Halter+Search: 88.1% on PW, 78.1% on EB; beats Proof+Answer and EntailmentWriter. Vs Proof-Only+Halter+Search: higher on PW, lower on EB Task 2 (72.9 vs 76.2%). Made-up facts ≤1% vs up to 60% for baselines. Random/incomplete context hurts SI far more than Proof+Answer and EntailmentWriter → answers use the trace. Halter's 'Unknown' raises precision.
limits: Correct steps not guaranteed (validity holds only if inferences are correct). Needs a given context and gold proofs for SFT. 7B only, two synthetic/science datasets. No code release mentioned.
relations: extends [[creswell2023selectioninference]]: fine-tunes Selection-Inference modules; adds learned halter and value-guided beam search

title: Selection-Inference: Exploiting Large Language Models for Interpretable Logical Reasoning
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:cot-reliance; signal:by-construction; lever:prompt-pipeline; lever:sft; updates:behavior; contribution:method; contribution:analysis; motivation:explainability; motivation:reasoning-quality; domain:logic; domain:open-qa; domain:mcq; domain:synthetic; scale:small; model:gopher-7b; model:gopher-280b
problem: LLMs weak at multi-step logic; CoT answer need not causally depend on its trace (grey zone near post-hoc rationale).
method: Selection-Inference (SI): frozen Gopher-7B, 5-shot. Selection picks context facts by log-likelihood; Inference sees only the selection (no question) → new fact → repeat. Also 50-task Gopher-family logic eval; SFT variant on ProofWriter.
findings: 10 tasks, generative: SI-7B 58.75% vs vanilla 2.94%, CoT 41.32%; beats 280B (vanilla 31.19%, CoT 44.03%). SFT-SI 78.95% on ProofWriter (prompted SI 57.93%); traces closer to gold proofs (Jaccard) than one-pass SFT. LLMs good at 1-step entailment, poor at multi-step. No accuracy cost.
limits: Trace causality by construction, never measured. Fixed step count, no halting. Selection is main failure point; gains shrink with depth. Context must be given. Gopher only; no code release mentioned.

title: Behavior Cue Reasoning: Monitorable Reasoning Improves Efficiency and Safety through Oversight
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:cot-reliance; signal:cot-intervention; signal:env-label; lever:sft; lever:architecture; updates:explanation; contribution:method; motivation:monitoring; motivation:scalable-oversight; motivation:efficiency; domain:math; domain:agentic; scale:small; model:qwen3-8b; model:glm-z1-9b; metric:forced-cue-adherence; metric:token-savings-vs-oracle; metric:monitor-f1; metric:safe-action-recovery
problem: Misaligned or wasteful behaviors stay hidden in CoT until the answer commits → monitors can't intervene mid-reasoning.
method: Working answers elicited by truncating the CoT, embedded as [answer]/[continue]/[stop] cues → SFT the actor; a weak non-reasoning monitor (RL/SFT) or a rule monitor acts at [answer] points.
findings: No acc cost (Qwen AIME 62.5→69.2). Forced-cue adherence varies by domain ([continue] 31–34% on AIME). Monitor on compressed answer progression prunes up to 50% of wasted AIME tokens; per-step decision points collapse. Rule monitor recovers a safe action in 80% of unsafe traces, success 46→96%. Code released.
limits: 8–9B only; one seed for monitor runs; short-answer domains; LLM safety monitor F1 weak; prompting/RL fail to induce cues; acc parity only at mid SFT checkpoints; [answer] fidelity to true working answer never tested.

title: Can LLMs Explain Themselves Counterfactually?
tags: source:trustme; object:posthoc-expl; reveals:decision-factors; signal:generic-cf; contribution:analysis; motivation:explainability; domain:classification; domain:math; scale:small; scale:mid; model:llama-3.1-8b; model:llama-3.3-70b; model:gemma-2-9b; model:gemma-2-27b; model:mistral-7b; model:deepseek-r1-distill-qwen-32b; metric:counterfactual-validity; eval:confound-control
problem: Do LLMs' self-generated counterfactual explanations (SCEs) actually flip their own prediction to the requested target label?
method: Predict → prompt an SCE for a target label (unconstrained / rationale-based / CoT) → re-predict on the SCE with vs. w/o chat history. 7 open LLMs (7–70B), 6 datasets (DiscrimEval, FolkTexts, SST2, Twitter-fin, MGNLI, GSM8K). Metrics: Gen, Val, edit distance.
findings: SCEs are mostly generated but often invalid; GSM8K Val mostly <20%. Chat history shifts Val (inflates it on GSM8K, FolkTexts; suggests target copying). Val tracks human-judged correctness only w/o context. Size, R1-distill and leaderboard rank give no consistent gain. CoT helps a little (avg Val 75 vs 69%). Code released.
limits: Open models ≤70B only; simple tasks with discrete or integer labels; human correctness check only on GSM8K (50/model, done by the authors); no fix tested.
relations: extends [[madsen2024self]]: broader SCE self-consistency test: generation rates, prompting variants, chat-history effect, hidden states | builds-on [[bhan2025did]]: uses its sentence-level mean embeddings for SCE drift; SCE clustering inspired by it

title: Split Personality Training: Revealing Latent Knowledge Through Alternate Personalities
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:self-report; reveals:hidden-behavior; reveals:misbehavior; signal:implanted-behavior; signal:judge; signal:planted-cf; lever:sft; lever:architecture; updates:explanation; contribution:method; motivation:auditing; domain:chat; scale:mid; eval:ood; eval:adversarial; eval:specificity; eval:privileged-access; eval:behavior-control; model:llama-3.3-70b; model:gemma-3-12b; model:qwen3-14b; model:qwen3-32b; model:gemma-3-27b; metric:detection-accuracy; metric:held-out-topic-accuracy; metric:prompt-swap-accuracy-gap
problem: Models trained to conceal reward hacking defeat black-box audits and direct questioning; need latent-knowledge access without changing deployed behavior.
method: SFT honest-persona LoRA, switched on only after the main response (split-personality token + intervention) → review + PASS/FAIL flag. Training labels: Claude Sonnet 4.5 comparing biased/unbiased-prompt responses, 11 topics. LoRA-mask variant.
findings: Auditing-game Llama-3.3-70B: 96% overall acc vs 0% self-admission, 72.2% base-Llama reviewer; also without reward-hack training topics; reviews name fictional biases. Beats probes on held-out topics (Qwen3-14B: 90.6 vs 81.0%). LoRA-mask worse. No deployed-model cost by construction.

title: Investigating Training and Generalization in Faithful Self-Explanations of Large Language Models
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:posthoc-expl; reveals:decision-factors; signal:generic-cf; lever:sft; updates:explanation; contribution:method; contribution:analysis; motivation:explainability; domain:classification; scale:small; scale:mid; eval:ood; model:tulu-2-7b; model:tulu-2-13b; metric:self-consistency-faithfulness
problem: Self-explanations (attribution/redaction/counterfactual) are often unfaithful; how can they be improved, and do gains transfer across styles?
method: Erasure attribution → most influential word → one-word pseudo-faithful explanation per style → LoRA continual SFT mixed with Tulu-2 instruct data; scored by Madsen self-consistency check on Sent140/SNLI/AGNews.
findings: Faithfulness ↑ in most task×style cells (13B Sent140 +0.115/+0.094/+0.292); prediction-only SFT mostly <0.01 or ↓. Cross-style transfer (13B, up to 0.781); unseen-task and per-word-count multi-word gains consistent only for attribution.

title: Output Supervision Can Obfuscate the Chain of Thought
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:misbehavior; reveals:planted-cue; signal:env-label; lever:rl-mechanics; lever:architecture; updates:explanation; contribution:method; contribution:negative-result; contribution:theory; motivation:monitoring; domain:math; domain:mcq; domain:agentic; scale:small; scale:mid; eval:optimization-pressure; model:qwen3-14b; model:qwen3-8b; model:qwen3-4b; metric:cot-monitor-detection-rate
problem: OpenAI/Baker propose training only against output monitors (no CoT access) to keep CoT monitorable. Can output-only supervision still obfuscate the CoT?
method: Policy-gradient decomposition → parametric and conditional "feedback spillover". REINFORCE on Qwen3 4B/8B/14B, penalizing a behavior in the output only (string match/regex or GPT-4.1/4.1-mini judge); the same check on the CoT measures spillover. 3 envs: polynomial derivative, hinted MMLU/hard math, terminal verifier-cheating. Mitigations: reward targeting (drops output-penalty gradient through CoT tokens), Mind & Face (separate CoT and output models).
findings: Output penalty → behavior vanishes from CoT too in all envs; in hint and terminal envs task reward stays high → obfuscated CoT. Mitigations, best combined, strongly cut spillover at high task reward in derivative and terminal envs (fully prevented in terminal). Hint env: unstable; on MMLU only combined prevents spillover, at 30% task-reward drop. Reward targeting: no extra compute. Code released.
limits: Only ≤14B Qwen3 models; toy envs. Derivative env needs in-context examples. Mind & Face trains two policy copies (costly). Hyperparameters not tuned per run type. Not tested on frontier models.
relations: contradicts [[baker2025monitoring]]: output-only monitor training still obfuscates CoT, contra proposed safe alternative | builds-on [[emmons2025chain]]: reuses polynomial derivative factoring environment | builds-on [[chen2025reasoning]]: reuses hinted MMLU questions setup to probe hint verbalization

title: When Chain of Thought is Necessary, Language Models Struggle to Evade Monitors
tags: source:trustme; object:cot; reveals:misbehavior; reveals:planted-cue; reveals:cot-reliance; reveals:hidden-info; signal:planted-cf; signal:cot-intervention; signal:env-label; contribution:analysis; motivation:monitoring; domain:mcq; domain:math; domain:agentic; scale:closed; eval:adversarial; eval:optimization-pressure; eval:specificity; factor:cot-necessity; model:gemini-2.5-pro; model:gemini-2.5-flash; model:gemini-2.0-flash; model:gemini-1.5-flash; model:gemini-1.5-pro; metric:monitor-recall; metric:suspicion-score; metric:evasion-success-rate; metric:unverbalized-hint-following
problem: Unfaithfulness results cast doubt on CoT monitoring; argue the key property is monitorability once CoT is necessary (CoT-as-computation vs -as-rationalization).
method: Replicate hint and forced-mistake setups at higher difficulty; stress-test Gemini CoT monitors against evasion via prompts, ART, RL (GPQA topic, oversight_pattern stealth, factorize_derivative).
findings: Complex hints → unverbalized hint use falls to no-hint baseline; hard math → answer follows corrupted CoT. Evasion needs human strategies or ART, costs accuracy; stronger monitors resist. RL vs monitor: evade+correct 0.5%→74.9% via early factoring + unforeseen targeted errors.

title: A Pragmatic Way to Measure Chain-of-Thought Monitorability

title: MONA: Myopic Optimization with Non-myopic Approval Can Mitigate Multi-step Reward Hacking
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:hidden-info; reveals:misbehavior; signal:planted-cf; signal:env-label; lever:rl-mechanics; updates:behavior; contribution:method; contribution:theory; motivation:monitoring; motivation:scalable-oversight; domain:code; domain:classification; domain:synthetic; domain:agentic; domain:social-bias; scale:closed; eval:optimization-pressure; model:gemini-1.5-flash; metric:counterfactual-impact; metric:ground-truth-return
problem: Multi-step reward hacks the overseer cannot detect, incl. reasoning encoded to evade a CoT/summary monitor → patching fails.
method: MONA: myopic (1-step) RL + overseer foresight-approval reward with no outcome info; vs ordinary RL (ORL) with identical step rewards. Gemini-1.5-Flash in 2-step coding (self-written tests) & loan (nationality-monitored summary → decision); gridworld camera tampering; causal-incentive theorem.
findings: ORL hacks in all envs: trivial tests; nationality hidden in summary sentiment, evades monitor (nationality swap drops reward), even with sign-flipped monitor reward. method: SFT on M0's counterfactual cue-ablation explanations ("would the answer change without the cue?") + KL behavior regularizer. Explanations scored against current-self vs M0 labels. title: AtManRL: Towards Faithful Reasoning via Differentiable Attention Saliency

problem: CoT may just accompany the answer; outcome-only RL doesn't enforce that the answer causally depends on it. Saliency: necessary, not sufficient, for faithfulness.
method: Per rollout, additive AtMan attention mask on CoT tokens init suppressed (c=-0.4), optimized 200 steps to restore answer log-prob → mean normalized mask (÷c) = saliency reward, added to GRPO outcome reward. Llama-3.2-3B, GSM8K/MMLU, vs outcome-only GRPO.
findings: CoT tokens -44% (GSM8K), -46% (MMLU). GSM8K CoTs denser (stop words -25%, numbers +48%, symbols +61%); MMLU composition shift small. Pass@4 -0.4%/+0.1% → no accuracy cost.

title: A Removal Based Approach to Improve LLM Faithfulness at Test-Time

method: Removal wrapper: an auxiliary LLM (Qwen3.5-27B) extracts the input's concepts, flags those the explanation does not credit and deletes them → target is re-queried in a fresh context. Also a Combined variant with modular prompting. Tested on hint-augmented MCQ and BBQ.

title: Are self-explanations from Large Language Models faithful?

method: Inference-only self-consistency checks, re-classified in a fresh session: a counterfactual must get the requested label; with the listed words (feature attribution) or self-redacted text masked as [REDACTED], the answer must be "unknown". Llama2-70B robust to prompt variants. Redaction ≈ FA → masking not OOD.

title: Walk the Talk? Measuring the Faithfulness of Large Language Model Explanations

title: A Positive Case for Faithfulness: LLM Self-Explanations Help Predict Model Behavior

title: On the Generalization of Steering Vectors for Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness

title: Logic-LM: Empowering Large Language Models with Symbolic Solvers for Faithful Logical Reasoning
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:cot-reliance; signal:by-construction; lever:prompt-pipeline; lever:architecture; lever:inference-time; updates:behavior; contribution:method; motivation:reasoning-quality; domain:logic; domain:mcq; scale:closed; model:gpt-3.5-turbo; model:text-davinci-003; model:gpt-4
problem: CoT conclusions may not follow from the stated chain (unfaithful reasoning) → errors on complex logic problems.
method: Few-shot LLM translates NL problem into LP/FOL/CSP/SAT → deterministic solver (Pyke, Prover9, python-constraint, Z3) derives answer → rule/LLM interpreter maps it back. Self-refiner repairs non-executable forms using solver error messages; otherwise falls back to CoT.

problem: Can LLMs report quantitative features of their internal decision processes (attribute weights in multi-attribute choice), and can training improve this?
method: SFT GPT-4o/4o-mini on choices of 100 agents with random attribute weights; logistic regression on choices → learned weights; prompt for weight reports without deciding. Then SFT on target-weight reports (2-fold, held-out contexts); test on native weights in 100 new contexts.

problem: Do LLM self-explanations let humans infer the model's outputs on related inputs (counterfactual simulatability)?
method: LLMs generate counterfactuals from the explanation; humans (StrategyQA) or GPT-4 (SHP) infer outputs via entailment → simulation precision (match w/ actual output) + generality (CF diversity). GPT-3.5/GPT-4 × CoT/post-hoc.

title: A Principled Approach to Chain-of-Thought Monitorability in Reasoning Models

problem: CoTs hide hint use and are verbose → hard to monitor. RL on a monitorability reward stalls: the base model rarely satisfies f(z), so the gradient is ~0.
method: Constrained opt (max f(z) s.t. reward ≥ base). Prompted Qwen2.5-7B rewrites R1-Distill-1.5B traces (verbalize hint / shorten) → keep reward-preserving, constraint-satisfying rewrite w/ max base likelihood → SFT.

title: Preventing Language Models From Hiding Their Reasoning

problem: Encoded reasoning (steganography in the CoT) could hide reasoning steps from readers → unfaithful CoT, weaker monitoring.
method: Demo: SFT GPT-3.5 on toy sycophancy task to encode an intermediate result in its intro sentence. Red-team eval: watermark and prompted LLM encoders hide random bits; GPT-3.5 paraphrases (± question context) + suspiciousness penalty. Capacity + win-rate on AlpacaEval, AQUA-RAT.
findings: Encoded CoT: 80% sycophantic vs 54% direct; random-intro control no gain. Paraphrasing almost always leaves <2 bits/answer (~3 bits/KB). AQUA-RAT: context-aware paraphrase keeps ~all of GPT-4's win-rate gain over GPT-3.5; AlpacaEval win-rate drops 8%. Code released.
limits: Stego only induced (SFT, prompts, watermarks); emergence under RL untested. Human-built schemes may over- or underestimate LLMs. 2 datasets; paraphraser untrained; +50% serial latency.

title: FaiRR: Faithful and Robust Deductive Reasoning over Natural Language
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:decision-factors; reveals:cot-reliance; signal:by-construction; signal:generic-cf; lever:architecture; lever:prompt-pipeline; lever:sft; updates:behavior; contribution:method; motivation:explainability; motivation:reasoning-quality; domain:logic; domain:synthetic; scale:small; eval:ood; model:roberta-large; model:t5-large
problem: Single-model proof+inference generators (ProofWriter) see the whole theory → inference may use premises beyond the stated proof → proofs possibly unfaithful.
method: FaiRR: RoBERTa-large rule selector → fact selector → T5-large composer that sees only the selected premises, iterated; the proof is a by-product of the selections; each module SFT'd on decomposed ProofWriter data.
findings: ≈PW-Iter on D0-D3 (EA 99.2 vs 99.8, small cost); more robust to subject perturbations (consistency 96.4 vs 87.6); 3.5× faster; errors localizable to a module; manual ablation: PW errs once irrelevant premises are added back. Code released.
limits: Synthetic rulebases, small models; early-stop errors → weaker on unseen depths (-3% proof acc vs PW-Iter on D5); slightly worse than PW-Iter on attribute perturbations; poor zero-shot on ParaRules.

title: Monitor Jailbreaking: Evading Chain-of-Thought Monitoring Without Encoded Reasoning

title: Structural Chain-of-Thought: Reasoning with Executable Computational Graphs
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:cot-reliance; signal:by-construction; signal:cot-intervention; lever:sft; lever:rl-reward; lever:architecture; updates:behavior; contribution:method; motivation:explainability; motivation:reasoning-quality; domain:math; domain:logic; scale:small; model:gemma-2-2b; model:llama-3.2-3b; model:falcon3-3b; model:qwen3-4b; metric:internal-external-gap; metric:f-strong; eval:confound-control

method: Model emits an executable JSON computational graph; answer = its deterministic execution. Graph SFT → Graph-Based GRPO (style, graded correctness, node-overlap or proof-F1 rewards; faithfulness runs also emit an answer, with answer and answer–graph consistency rewards). 4 models ≤4B, 5 math/proof datasets.

title: Balancing Faithfulness and Performance in Reasoning via Multi-Listener Soft Execution

problem: Contextual (CoT/input perturbation) and parametric (unlearning) CoT-faithfulness metrics compared only descriptively; does optimizing one transfer to the others?
method: FaithMATE: best/worst of 40 sampled CoTs under one metric → SFT or DPO (LoRA); measure gain transfer δ on 6 metrics (4 Lanham corruptions, CC-SHAP, FUR). Gemma3-4B/Qwen2.5-7B/Llama3.1-8B; OpenBookQA, LogiQA. Plus task-arithmetic merging.

EA+FT merging amplifies gains; merging hurts Paraphrasing.

title: ReFIne: A Framework for Trustworthy Large Reasoning Models with Reliability, Faithfulness, and Interpretability
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:planted-cue; reveals:stated-plan; reveals:cot-reliance; signal:planted-cf; signal:judge; signal:cot-intervention; lever:sft; lever:rl-reward; lever:architecture; updates:explanation; contribution:method; motivation:explainability; motivation:reliability; domain:math; domain:mcq; scale:small; eval:ood; eval:human-study; model:qwen3-1.7b; model:qwen3-4b; model:qwen3-8b; model:deepseek-r1-distill-llama-8b; metric:disclosure-faithfulness; metric:commitment-faithfulness

method: SFT on tagged traces (understanding→facts→plan→think→answer→self-assessment) → GRPO rewarding correctness, format, cross-section refs, calibrated confidence. Vs matched Plain (correctness-only GRPO).
findings: Qwen3-1.7/4/8B: interpretability +44.0%, faithfulness +18.8% (professor-hint disclosure up), reliability +42.4%; commitment faithfulness 0.90–1.00 (QwQ), 0.83–0.94 (MTurk); acc ≈ Plain, 1.16× shorter. Transfers to DS-R1-Llama-8B. Code released.

title: LIFT: Likelihood-Based Intervention Faithfulness Training

problem: CoT answers often don't causally depend on the stated steps; prior fixes need human labels/filtering or symbolic solvers.
method: Swap each step for a domain-matched irrelevant fact (Wikidata/arithmetic corpus, style-rewritten), regenerate, score answer log-prob drop → score-weighted LoRA SFT on post-intervention continuations + gold-answer term (η) + KL to base.

Claims no significant acc cost (yet Mistral GSM8K 0.41 vs 0.50). No answer supervision → more faithful, big acc drop. Code/data in supplement.

title: Entailer: Answering Questions with Faithful and Truthful Chains of Reasoning
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:cot-reliance; reveals:decision-factors; signal:by-construction; signal:judge; lever:prompt-pipeline; lever:sft; lever:inference-time; updates:behavior; updates:explanation; contribution:method; contribution:benchmark; motivation:explainability; domain:mcq; scale:mid; eval:human-study; eval:ood; model:t5-11b; metric:human-judged-conclusion-follows; metric:human-judged-premise-correctness
problem: CoT/explanations may be unfaithful (answer doesn't follow) and untruthful (model doesn't believe its own premises).
method: T5-11B fine-tuned on EntailmentBank + new crowd-labeled entailments (incl. negatives); backward-chains from each answer hypothesis, overgenerates premises, keeps steps the model self-verifies (premises + entailment); answer = top-scoring proof.

limits: Faithful only by answer selection; belief = "yes" to "Is X true?". Near-tautologies, invalid steps; ~360 s/question; one model, science MCQ.

title: On the Hardness of Faithful Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Large Language Models
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:cot-reliance; signal:cot-intervention; lever:prompt-pipeline; lever:sft; lever:steering; updates:behavior; contribution:negative-result; contribution:analysis; motivation:explainability; domain:mcq; domain:math; domain:logic; scale:small; scale:closed; model:llama-3-8b; model:gpt-3.5-turbo; model:gpt-4; metric:early-answering-aoc
problem: Can standard steering tools (ICL, fine-tuning, activation editing) make the CoT faithful, i.e. make the answer depend on it?
method: ICL and LoRA SFT on self-generated (Q, CoT, A) triplets picked uniformly or by faithfulness (deterministic/stochastic, correct-only variants); ITI-style editing of probe-selected heads. Faithfulness = per-instance early-answering AOC. AQuA, LogiQA, TruthfulQA.
findings: ICL/SFT: small gains that depend on dataset and model, often with an acc drop (~20% vs GTA baseline, Llama SFT on TruthfulQA). Text says faithful demos beat uniform ones; appendix tables mixed. Steering: no significant gain; best heads/alpha/K differ by dataset. GPT-4 is the most accurate and the least faithful.

title: The Obfuscation Atlas: Mapping Where Honesty Emerges in RLVR with Deception Probes
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:output; reveals:misbehavior; signal:env-label; signal:interp-tool; lever:rl-reward; lever:rl-mechanics; updates:behavior; contribution:analysis; contribution:theory; contribution:benchmark; contribution:negative-result; motivation:monitoring; motivation:scalable-oversight; domain:code; scale:small; scale:mid; eval:optimization-pressure; eval:ood; model:llama-3-8b; model:gemma-3-12b; model:gemma-3-27b; model:llama-3-70b; metric:honest-policy-rate; metric:original-model-probe-score; metric:representation-change; metric:probe-auc
problem: Training against white-box deception probes may teach evasion, not honesty; prior obfuscation evidence only from artificial harmful-output setups.
method: MBPP-Honeypot RLVR (1 visible test + length penalty → hardcoding); GRPO + off-domain deception-probe penalty; KL × penalty sweep; probe score split: original-model vs representation change.
findings: Outcomes: honest, blatant, obfuscated policy (evasive text, e.g. justifications; low KL + weak penalty), obfuscated activations (RL drift, even w/o probe; PG adds no activation pressure, probe gradients do). High KL + high penalty → honest, no capability cost. Code/models released.
limits: High KL often impractical at scale; obfuscated policies hard to detect; single-turn MBPP, ≤70B; richer hacks (test tampering) untested.

title: Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think: Unfaithful Explanations in Chain-of-Thought Prompting
tags: source:trustme; object:cot; reveals:planted-cue; reveals:decision-factors; signal:planted-cf; signal:generic-cf; contribution:analysis; motivation:explainability; motivation:monitoring; domain:mcq; domain:logic; domain:social-bias; scale:closed; model:text-davinci-003; model:claude-1.0; metric:biased-context-accuracy-drop; metric:unfaithfulness-explained-by-bias

method: Biasing features the CoT never mentions (Answer-is-Always-A, Suggested Answer) on 13 BBH tasks; BBQ with swapped weak evidence. GPT-3.5 & Claude 1.0, ZS/FS, CoT vs No-CoT.
findings: Bias verbalized in 1/426 explanations. Accuracy drops up to 36% (ZS); FS CoT less unfaithful. 73% of sampled unfaithful CoTs argue for the biased answer; 15% have no obvious errors. BBQ: up to 62.5% of unfaithful pairs stereotype-aligned (50% = unbiased). Debiasing prompt helps Claude. Code released.

title: Teaching Models to Verbalize Reward Hacking in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
tags: source:trustme; source:faith-improvement; object:cot; reveals:planted-cue; reveals:misbehavior; signal:planted-cf; lever:sft; updates:explanation; contribution:method; motivation:monitoring; domain:mcq; scale:small; eval:later-rl; eval:ood; eval:specificity; model:llama-3.1-8b; metric:effective-cue-influence-rate; metric:hint-verbalization-rate; metric:balanced-accuracy
problem: RL-learned reward hacks (exploiting prompt cues) go unverbalized in CoT → CoT monitors miss them.
method: VFT: SFT on CoTs minimally edited (Claude 4 Sonnet) to credit planted cues (2 cues) → GRPO rewarding cue-aligned wrong MMLU answers incl. held-out cues; vs BCT, RL-only.
findings: Post-RL undetected hacks (ECR) 6% vs 88% RL-only, 99% BCT; verbalization 8%→43% (VFT)→94% (RL). Holds, smaller gap, on non-amplified cues (ECR 15% vs 63-66%). Pre-RL specificity 96-97%. MMLU acc 73→70% after VFT; post-RL ≈ RL-only (63 vs 65%).

title: Measuring Chain of Thought Faithfulness by Unlearning Reasoning Steps
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:decision-factors; signal:param-intervention; contribution:metric; contribution:analysis; motivation:explainability; domain:mcq; scale:small; eval:human-study; model:llama-3-8b; model:llama-3.2-3b; model:mistral-7b; model:phi-3-mini; metric:ff-hard; metric:ff-soft
problem: Context perturbation tests measure self-consistency, not parametric faithfulness: models can recover erased steps from weights.
method: FUR (PFF instance): unlearn each CoT step's content words (NPO+KL, FF2) → no-CoT answer flips (ff-hard) or loses probability (ff-soft)? Controls: efficacy, specificity, MMLU. 4 LMs, 5 MCQA sets.
findings: MMLU ~unchanged; answers often flip, mostly more than Add-mistake; efficacy tracks ff-hard (r=0.889). Post-unlearning CoTs argue for other answers (GPT-4o-mini judge). ff-soft vs human plausibility r=0.15. Code released.

title: Markovian Transformers for Informative Language Modeling
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:cot-reliance; reveals:hidden-info; reveals:correctness; signal:cot-intervention; signal:by-construction; lever:architecture; lever:rl-reward; lever:rl-mechanics; updates:behavior; updates:explanation; contribution:method; motivation:explainability; domain:math; domain:mcq; domain:text-continuation; scale:small; eval:held-out-evaluator; model:llama-3.1-8b; model:mistral-7b; model:qwen3-4b; model:phi-3.5-mini; metric:perturbation-fragility; metric:cross-model-informativeness
problem: Standard CoT is not load-bearing: the answer can bypass the reasoning, so the CoT may not reflect the decision.
method: Markovian bottleneck: answer predicted from length-capped CoT alone, question hidden. GRPO-style RL on ln P(ans|CoT) vs a frozen-baseline CoT, actor-reward grads, KL to base; LoRA.
findings: GSM8K 19.6→57.1%, ARC 36.1→79.9%; mean ≈3–4 pp below Non-Markovian GRPO (MMLU 13 pp). Larger drops under CoT perturbation than Non-Markovian (Wiki, most QA; not arithmetic). Llama CoTs help Mistral/Phi/GPT-2 predict GSM8K answers. Code released.

title: PINTO: Faithful Language Reasoning Using Prompt-Generated Rationales
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:cot-reliance; signal:cot-intervention; signal:simulatability; lever:prompt-pipeline; lever:sft; updates:behavior; contribution:method; motivation:reasoning-quality; motivation:explainability; domain:mcq; scale:small; scale:mid; eval:ood; model:t5-base; model:roberta-large; model:gpt-neox-20b; metric:leakage-adjusted-simulatability; metric:perturbed-rationale-acc-drop
problem: Rationale-augmented reasoners can ignore or misuse rationales (shortcuts) → rationales unfaithful; self-rationalization needs >100B LMs or costly rationale annotation.
method: Frozen GPT-NeoX-20B prompted (7 demos) → choice-specific rationales; T5-base reasoner fine-tuned w/ counterfactual regularization: label-smoothed (low-confidence) targets when rationale masked or 30% tokens replaced.
findings: Best ID acc in most cases, best OOD among rationale methods; T5: higher LAS except OBQA (CSQA 24.22 vs 18.75 std); larger acc drop under swapped rationales; biggest gain from human rationales. Acc rises, no cost. Code released.

title: SCOTT: Self-Consistent Chain-of-Thought Distillation
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:cot-reliance; signal:generic-cf; signal:cot-intervention; lever:sft; updates:behavior; updates:explanation; contribution:method; motivation:explainability; domain:mcq; domain:classification; scale:small; scale:mid; eval:human-study; model:t5-3b; model:gpt-neox-20b; metric:leakage-adjusted-simulatability; metric:rationale-perturbation-sensitivity; metric:rationale-refinement-gain
problem: Distilled CoT rationales are vacuous (teacher hallucinates) and ignored (student answers via question→answer shortcuts) → rationale-answer inconsistency.
method: GPT-NeoX-20B teacher rationalizes gold answers via contrastive decoding (vs empty/wrong answer) → T5-3b student SFT with factual + counterfactual loss (wrong-answer rationale → wrong answer).
findings: CD-wrong teacher most consistent. CD students generally higher LAS than CoT prompting, greedy/human-rationale students; counterfactual loss adds more. Comparable acc (human-rationale student slightly higher). More perturbation-sensitive, bigger refinement gains. Larger students more accurate, less faithful; gains hold across sizes. Code released.
limits: Extra teacher forward pass + counterfactual data. LAS needs T5-large simulator. Knowledge-intensive QA only; perturbation/refinement on CSQA, CREAK only.

title: Causally-Enhanced Reinforcement Policy Optimization
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:cot-reliance; signal:interp-tool; lever:rl-reward; updates:behavior; contribution:method; motivation:reasoning-quality; domain:math; domain:mcq; domain:logic; domain:open-qa; domain:code; domain:professional; scale:small; eval:ood; model:llama-3-8b; model:llama-3.2-3b; model:phi-3.5-mini; model:qwen3-4b-thinking-2507; model:qwen3-1.7b; metric:jacobian-coherence-score
problem: Outcome-only RL → correct answers paired with spurious/unfaithful CoT; shortcut learning, reward hacking.
method: CE-PO: Jacobian influence scores for Z→X, X→Y, direct Z→Y (prompt→rationale→answer), hardened by projecting out token-shuffled counterfactual subspace; power-mean fused with BERTScore → PPO/GRPO reward.
findings: +5.49 pts avg acc over vanilla (up to 9.58); both CE variants beat BERTScore-PPO/GRPO on avg for all 5 models, 4 test sets; OOD gains (Qwen3-4B only). Unhardened or partial Jacobian reward → length hacking. Scores higher on judge-correct samples. Code released.
limits: ≤8B only. Faithfulness gauged only by own Jacobian scores; no independent CoT test; abstract's unfaithful-CoT and perturbation-robustness claims not directly tested. First-order proxy, not true DCE. Acc via GPT-4o-mini judge; ablations and OOD on one model each.

title: Enhancing the Outcome Reward-based RL Training of MLLMs with Self-Consistency Sampling
tags: source:trustme; object:cot; reveals:cot-reliance; reveals:reasoning-validity; signal:cot-intervention; signal:judge; lever:rl-reward; updates:behavior; contribution:method; motivation:reasoning-quality; domain:multimodal; domain:mcq; domain:math; scale:small; eval:ood; model:qwen2.5-vl-7b; model:qwen2.5-vl-3b; model:internvl3-8b; metric:flawed-reasoning-correct-answer-rate; metric:distinct-answers-after-truncation
problem: Outcome-reward RL on multimodal MCQ rewards lucky guesses after a faulty CoT like genuine reasoning → unfaithful traces reinforced.
method: SCS: truncate rollout, resample continuations under Gaussian image noise; answer agreement → consistency reward, added to accuracy + format rewards in RLOO, GRPO, REINFORCE++ variants.
findings: Qwen2.5-VL-7B avg acc (6 benchmarks): +7.7 pp RLOO, +0.9–2.0 pp others; +3.2 / +1.6 pp on 3B / InternVL3-8B (RLOO). Vs. base model, correct answers with flawed reasoning ~15% rarer (human 25.0→21.2 per 100; o3-mini, Gemini agree). Code released.

title: Self-Critique and Refinement for Faithful Natural Language Explanations
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:posthoc-expl; reveals:decision-factors; signal:generic-cf; lever:prompt-pipeline; lever:inference-time; updates:explanation; contribution:method; motivation:explainability; domain:mcq; domain:classification; scale:small; eval:behavior-control; model:llama-3.1-8b; model:mistral-7b-v0.3; model:qwen2.5-7b; model:falcon3-7b; metric:counterfactual-unfaithfulness-rate
problem: Post-hoc NLEs leave out the input words that actually drive the prediction.
method: Training-free self-refine loop (SR-NLE): answer → NLE → feedback (free-text critique, or top-5 important words via prompting/attention/IG) → refine, up to 3 rounds. Scored with the Atanasova CF word-insertion test. 4 7–8B models on ComVE, ECQA and e-SNLI.
findings: Avg unfaithfulness 54.81% → 36.02% (IWF-Attn). IWF beats NLF in every setting; NLF beats self-consistency sampling only on avg. Prompted IWF ≈ attribution IWF. Largest gain in round 1. Answers fixed, so no acc change. Code released.
limits: Single string-match CF metric. Refined NLEs get longer. Random-word feedback ≈ IWF (e-SNLI). Post-hoc NLEs only, <10B models. IG is costly.

title: CASE: Causal Alignment and Structural Enforcement for Improving Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:cot-reliance; signal:cot-intervention; signal:generic-cf; lever:sft; lever:architecture; updates:behavior; contribution:method; contribution:theory; motivation:explainability; domain:mcq; domain:logic; scale:small; eval:ood; model:llama-3.1-8b; model:qwen3-8b; model:deepseek-r1-distill-qwen-7b; metric:filler-tokens; metric:early-answering-aoc; metric:indirect-effect; metric:direct-effect
problem: Answer can bypass the CoT via a direct instruction→answer (Z→Y) shortcut.
method: Standard CoT SFT plus answer-only loss on counterfactual-CoT, biased-instruction and empty-instruction data; inference-time mask blocks answer→instruction attention. Mutual-information bound analysis. Three 7–8B models; ARC, StrategyQA, LogiQA.
findings: Best G-mean of FT/EA/CIE/CDE in all 12 settings: +37% avg vs per-setting strongest baseline (incl. untuned base), +61% in cross-dataset transfer. Avg acc 74.88 vs 74.80%. SFT mainly lifts CIE/CDE; mask lifts FT/EA. Code released.

title: MonitorBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Chain-of-Thought Monitorability in Large Language Models
tags: source:trustme; object:cot; reveals:decision-factors; reveals:planted-cue; reveals:misbehavior; reveals:internal-strategy; signal:planted-cf; signal:by-construction; signal:env-label; contribution:benchmark; contribution:analysis; motivation:monitoring; domain:mcq; domain:open-qa; domain:math; domain:logic; domain:code; domain:agentic; domain:synthetic; scale:mid; scale:large; scale:closed; eval:adversarial; eval:monitor-scope; model:qwen3-14b; model:qwen3-235b-a22b; model:gpt-oss-120b; model:gpt-5; model:gemini-3-flash; model:claude-sonnet-4.5; metric:monitorability-score

method: 1,514 instances / 19 tasks: cue & goal injection, dual objectives, impossible tasks, necessary steps. Qwen3-32B monitor, 3 scopes (CoT/action/all). Monitorability = flag rate, TE-normalized for injections. 8 LLMs. 2 prompt stress tests (direct concealment, monitor-aware evasion).
findings: High when factor shapes reasoning, low when it only sets the answer (Cue-Answer, deception). More capable → less monitorable (r −0.87 to −0.39). CoT-only beats action-only by ~24%. Stress tests cut Cue-Answer ~27%, via omission not obfuscation. Code released.

title: Monitorability as a Free Gift: How RLVR Spontaneously Aligns Reasoning
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:planted-cue; reveals:cot-reliance; reveals:misbehavior; signal:planted-cf; signal:cot-intervention; factor:outcome-rl; contribution:analysis; motivation:monitoring; domain:mcq; domain:math; domain:code; domain:logic; scale:small; model:deepseek-r1-distill-qwen-1.5b; model:qwen3-4b; metric:g-mean-squared; metric:draft-reliance; metric:draft-answer-consistency; eval:ood; eval:specificity; eval:scaling

method: GRPO (task+format reward) on Math/Code/Science/IF data & mixes, DS-R1-Qwen-1.5B & Qwen3-4B; track hint g-mean² (Qwen2.5-32B monitor), D2A draft-swap, entropy, attention; ablate train length, difficulty.

title: Faithful Logical Reasoning via Symbolic Chain-of-Thought

problem: NL CoT imprecise for logic; solver offloading (Logic-LM) brittle to translation errors and info loss, and gives little explanation.
method: Few-shot, LLM-only pipeline: translate to FOL/CO → plan → solve with symbolic rules over hybrid NL+symbolic premises → verifier checks translation & each step, refines.

problem: Introspection adapters (IAs) have mainly been tested on deliberately implanted behaviors. Real fine-tunes shift alignment as side effects that nobody labeled.
method: 213 HF PEFT fine-tunes of Qwen3-14B/Gemma3-12B; LLM-judge-scored harmful-compliance shift vs base on 13 safety categories → 5-way labels + LLM-written reference reports; SFT (+DPO for free-form) IAs; DAIA adapter processes base output & fine-tuning delta in separate branches.
