title: Outcome Rewards Do Not Guarantee Verifiable or Causally Important Reasoning
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:cot-reliance; reveals:correctness; signal:cot-intervention; signal:judge; lever:sft; lever:rl-reward; updates:behavior; updates:explanation; contribution:metric; contribution:analysis; contribution:method; motivation:explainability; motivation:monitoring; domain:math; domain:logic; domain:synthetic; scale:small; eval:later-rl; eval:optimization-pressure; model:qwen2.5-1.5b; model:qwen2.5-3b; model:qwen2.5-7b; model:llama-3.2-3b; metric:causal-importance-of-reasoning; metric:sufficiency-of-reasoning
problem: Does outcome-reward RLVR produce CoT that the model actually uses and that a verifier can check?
method: CIR: answer-prob. shift under CoT truncation (avg JS div.). SR: gpt-4o-mini's answer from answer-stripped CoT unchanged when question added. GRPO, 40 ReasoningGym tasks. Fixes: SFT on 2–512 o3-mini traces before RLVR; CIR/SR aux rewards.
findings: RLVR ↑acc, but CIR ↓ on 19/40 tasks, SR ↓ on 17/40; both reliably ↑ only if acc gain >50 pts. No-CoT training ≈ same acc on low-CIR/SR tasks. SFT & aux rewards ↑CIR, SR (aux: also stricter SR−); aux keeps RLVR-level acc, large-n SFT ↑acc. Code released.
limits: Models ≤7B. SR binary, permissive; one seed for SR reward. Aux rewards don't ↑acc where base acc ≈0; lexical richness ↓ vs SFT. RLVR drop not universal: on MATH L5, CIR & SR ↑.
relations: builds-on [[lanham2023measuring]]: CIR turns truncation/early-answering into an averaged JS-divergence score | builds-on [[kirchner2024proververifier]]: SR operationalizes its legibility/verifiability notion ('inspired by'); no prover-verifier training

title: Is Chain-of-Thought Really Not Explainability? Chain-of-Thought Can Be Faithful without Hint Verbalization

title: Evaluating and Improving LLM Self-Modeling
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:self-prediction; object:posthoc-expl; reveals:decision-factors; reveals:planted-cue; signal:generic-cf; signal:planted-cf; lever:rl-reward; lever:sft; updates:explanation; contribution:benchmark; contribution:method; motivation:explainability; motivation:auditing; domain:math; domain:code; domain:social-bias; domain:mcq; domain:safety-refusal; domain:agentic; scale:small; scale:mid; model:llama-3.1-8b; model:qwen3-8b; model:gpt-oss-20b; model:qwen3-4b; model:qwen3-32b; model:deepseek-v3.1; metric:self-modeling-skill; metric:self-modeling-raw-score; eval:ood; eval:privileged-access; eval:behavior-control
problem: Do LLM self-reports predict their own behavior (e.g. "would this edit flip my answer?")? Even frontier models fail simple counterfactuals.
method: 9-task benchmark on GSM8K/HumanEval/WildGuardTest/BBQ. GT = the model's own sampled behavior on original or perturbed prompts. Skill = score minus dummy-predictor baseline. Perturb→verify→revise data from ~100 HF datasets + multi-turn BLOOM → LoRA RL.
findings: 18 models far from ceiling (best +0.147). Multitask RL raises skill in 3 families (Qwen3 4B–32B too), with partial cross-task transfer; SFT collapses OOD. No consistent own-model advantage → no clear evidence of introspection. MMLU-Pro −0.051 to +0.026. Code released.
limits: Text-only behavioral labels, not mechanism. Much of the gain is format compliance (Llama, GPT-OSS). Downstream red-team/prompt-engineering benefits are small.

title: How the Audit Rule Shapes Faithful Factor Explanations in LLMs

problem: Budget-limited counterfactual audits of factor-importance self-reports; report-dependent auditing rewards suppressing factors, even under a proper score.
method: Verification game + Counterfactual Brier Score (report vs. flip rate, n=3); proofs for proportional, bonus, report-independent, floor audits. Rational best-response agent + 5 API LLMs; BBQ, GSM8K, HotpotQA, StrategyQA.
findings: Proportional: rational agent suppresses 36.9% of factors; bonus → inflation; report-independent 100% truthful, 10% floor ~98%; same pattern with log/spherical scores. LLMs follow explicit reward tables, much less without; multi-round suppression 0.15 (proportional) vs 0.08 (report-indep.), 2 models.
limits: Directional LLM evidence, not equilibrium; API models, temp 0; no training; single-factor perturbations miss interactions. No code reported.

title: A Necessary Step toward Faithfulness: Measuring and Improving Consistency in Free-Text Explanations
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:posthoc-expl; reveals:decision-factors; signal:simulatability; signal:generic-cf; lever:preference; updates:explanation; contribution:metric; contribution:method; contribution:analysis; motivation:explainability; domain:classification; scale:small; scale:mid; eval:behavior-control; model:mistral-7b-v0.3; model:llama-2-13b; model:yi-1.5-9b; metric:pex-consistency; metric:simulatability-f1
problem: Post-hoc free-text expls often back both a prediction and its negation → cannot be faithful (contrastive consistency as a necessary condition).
method: PEX = weight of evidence: shift in the model's own log-odds for its answer once the expl is in context. Rank 80 sampled expls per input → DPO on top- vs bottom-PEX pairs. Faithfulness proxy = student simulatability F1 (Pruthi 2022). Opinion-spam classification (TripAdvisor, Amazon).
findings: 62–86% of expls inconsistent (PEX<0). Over SFT expls, DPO raises PEX 43.1–292.3% and student simulation F1 by 1.5–9.7 pts. PEX fairly robust to prompt format. Code released.
limits: Needs output probabilities (no black-box models). Faithfulness checked at system level only. Binary opinion-spam tasks only, 7–13B. PEX is necessary, not sufficient. DPO gains capped by best sampled expl (Mistral PEX stays <0).

title: Conceptual Steganography
tags: source:search-2026-10-14; object:cot; reveals:hidden-info; signal:by-construction; lever:inference-time; updates:explanation; contribution:attack; contribution:method; contribution:negative-result; motivation:monitoring; domain:math; domain:mcq; scale:large; model:gpt-oss-120b; model:deepseek-v4-flash; model:qwen3.5-122b-a10b; model:mimo-v2.5-pro; metric:decoding-success; metric:bit-error-rate; eval:adversarial
problem: Covert payloads in CoT (encoded reasoning); paraphrasing assumed to close stego channels because they ride on surface words.
method: Prompted pipeline: segment CoT into steps, rewrite each to show/omit a reasoning behavior (e.g. anticipate_failure) per bit → same-model paraphraser → LLM decoder; vs matched keyword channel; 4 open models, MATH-500/GPQA. Defense: strategy-aware paraphraser.
findings: After paraphrase, concept beats keyword in all 8 model×dataset cells (up to +35.8 pts msg acc), via lower bit error. Answers recoverable from encoded/paraphrased CoT within ~1%; no-CoT costs 20–43 pts. Strategy-aware paraphrase: bit error 0.2–2.4% → 27–37%, msg acc −58–72 pts.
limits: Encoder prompted, not trained/emergent. Main results: strongest strategy only; others weaker (single-channel tests MiMo only). No stealth test. Defense: 1 strategy, GPQA, 3 models. LLM decoder; single seed.
relations: builds-on [[roger2023preventing]]: adopts its content-preserving paraphraser as the standard defense against encoded reasoning | contradicts [[roger2023preventing]]: claimed paraphrasing largely closes the channel; behavior-level carriers survive standard paraphrase
